title: Stochastic adaptive optimization with unreliable inputs: A unified framework for high-probability complexity analysis
contribution: One adaptive framework covering trust region and line search, with high-probability iteration complexity O(eps^-2) when gradients are arbitrarily corrupted with probability above 1/2 and function values carry heavy-tailed or corrupted noise; the tail of the stopping time is exponential or polynomial depending on the zeroth-order oracle.
problem_entry: Weakens the near-universal assumption that oracles are accurate with probability above 1/2 each iteration (only GRVZ18 relaxed it, and it needs exact function values); the regime is justified by arithmetic: 19% clean minibatches, 64% corrupted FD gradients (pp. 1-2, 5).
key_idea: Use function-value estimates to guard against badly corrupted gradients, and make the step-size random walk drift upward via asymmetric factors: p ln g_inc + (1-p) ln g_dec > 0, i.e. p > 1/(m+1) (pp. 2, 15).
assumptions: L-smooth, bounded below; SZO (bounded mean and q-th centred moment of the error) or CZO (error <= eps_f w.p. 1-delta0, <= eps_f+eps_c always); SFO accurate to r(alpha) w.p. 1-delta1, arbitrary otherwise; algorithm-class Assumptions 2-3 (small+true => successful; large+successful => decrease h(eps)) (pp. 1-4, 12).
proof_devices: deterministic counting of true/successful/large iterations from step-size dynamics (Lemmas 2-3)
contradiction on the intersection of two events: Azuma-Hoeffding on sum of I_k and concentration of accumulated noise (Theorem 1)
Fuk-Nagaev inequality for q-th-moment noise, giving a polynomial tail; Chebyshev, Bernstein or Hoeffding for the other cases
general theorem plus per-method verification lemmas (TR Lemmas 4-5, LS Lemmas 6-7)
expected complexity and a.s. convergence obtained by summing tail bounds
positioning: Extends the group's own line (CS17, BCS21, PS20, JSX24, JSX25, BCMS19, CBS24, SX23); names GRVZ18's key limitation (exact function values); one sentence criticises ADAM and AdaGrad; recovers JSX24 as a special case (pp. 2, 5, 22).
writing: Numeric motivating examples before definitions; three bold contribution bullets with first-ever claims; a discussion paragraph after the main theorem turns the condition p > p_m into a parameter rule; sparse hedging (pp. 1-2, 6, 15).
limits_future: p is usually unknown and must be lower-bounded conservatively; the reachable eps is floored at order max{eps_g, sqrt(eps_f)}; no experiments and no future-work list (pp. 15, 22).

quotes.text: The key idea is to leverage function value information to ensure reliability when gradient estimates are severely corrupted.
In such a regime, the local model provided to the algorithm is more likely to be misleading than helpful in any given iteration.

title: On Complexity of Model-Based Derivative-Free Methods
contribution: First complexity bounds for Powell-style geometry-correcting model-based trust-region DFO without a criticality step: O(n^2 eps^-2) function evaluations, matching finite-difference TR, with a tightness example on the poisedness dependence, and O(nq eps^-2) in Haar-random subspaces.
problem_entry: A practice-theory gap: Powell-style methods are arguably the most effective in practice, but their complexity is unknown and existing theory needs a criticality step that departs from the algorithms (p. 1).
key_idea: Replace the criticality step with the acceptance test ||g_k|| >= eta2*Delta_k from stochastic TR; never shrink Delta on geometry-correcting iterations; count those iterations with a combinatorial potential; take Lambda = 1+O(1/n) (pp. 2-3, 7-11).
assumptions: C^1 with L-Lipschitz gradient, bounded below; exact or bounded-noise zeroth-order oracle; fraction of Cauchy decrease and bounded model Hessian; the subspace part needs an exact oracle and alignment probability theta > 1/2 (pp. 2-3, 5, 13, 17).
proof_devices: small-radius-implies-success and success-implies-C2*Delta^2 decrease lemmas giving a radius lower bound and counting (Lemmas 2.4-2.8)
radius decreased only when the model is certified fully linear, which gives the lower bound without fully-linear models at every iteration (Lemma 3.4)
growth of an orthogonal-set potential bounds consecutive geometry-correcting steps by 3n (Thm 3.6)
trace(A)+trace(A^-1) eigenvalue bound for ||Y^-T D|| improving the error bound to O(sqrt(n)) scaling (Thm 4.3)
Sherman-Morrison construction of a Lambda-poised set showing the bound is tight (Thm 4.6)
volume ratio with Hadamard inequality giving O(p log p) correcting calls for a general basis (Thm 5.1)
Beta law of the Haar projection with Paley-Zygmund giving alignment probability 243/443 (Lemma 6.7)
Cartis-Scheinberg 2018 stochastic-process argument for E[K_eps] <= 2theta/(2theta-1)^2 (...) (Thm 6.13)
positioning: DFO taxonomy (direct search, FD/simplex gradient, model-based TR); criticises the criticality step of the IDFO book (co-authored) and improves its poisedness bound; subspace competitors are Cartis-Roberts (O(n^2/eps^2)) and Kozak et al. (O(n/eps^2)) (pp. 1-2, 9, 13).
writing: Parity claim flagged as for-the-first-time in the abstract; a ladder of algorithms reusing Lemmas 2.4-2.5; one-line interpretations after theorems; visible drafting traces (leaked label, typos) (pp. 1-3, 11, 19).
limits_future: The subspace analysis needs an exact oracle; general-basis kappa_eg may not be optimal; underdetermined models are not analysed; future work: noisy subspaces, JL embeddings with the new bounds, other subspace generators, practical refinements (pp. 9, 13, 16-19).

Thus nothing is lost by employing Algorithm 2, aside from additional linear algebra costs of maintaining the Lagrange polynomials.

title: ProxSTORM--A Stochastic Trust-Region Algorithm for Nonsmooth Optimization
contribution: ProxSTORM extends STORM to f+phi (smooth nonconvex f, convex prox-friendly phi) with a.s. limit convergence and O(eps^-2) expected complexity; it also sharpens STORM by contracting only reduction differences, so O(Delta^-2) samples suffice under common random numbers; tested on l1-regularised HIGGS training and stochastic topology optimisation.
problem_entry: Merges a deterministic inexact proximal TR (whose errors must vanish deterministically, while real inexactness is stochastic) with STORM (stochastic, but smooth only) (pp. 1-2).
key_idea: Keep STORM's logic, swap the gradient for the proximal-gradient step h_k, keep phi exact, and state the function-value contract as |ared - cred| <= eta*pred (pp. 3-7).
assumptions: phi proper closed convex with an exact prox; f L-smooth; bounded model curvature; P(accurate model) >= alpha; P(accurate reduction | half-step filtration) >= beta; Assumption 5 on expected increase; alpha*beta > 1/2 (pp. 1-8, 15).
proof_devices: potential Psi_k = nu(f+phi) + (1-nu)Delta^2 with expected decrease -Theta*Delta^2 (Lemma 10)
partition on B_k and the accuracy events; offset the worst-case positive ||h||Delta term with the best-case negative term (weight alpha*beta)
half-step filtration F_{k-1/2} separating model and reduction randomness
submartingale W_k with +-1 increments compared with log_gamma Delta_k for liminf convergence (Thm 19)
Lipschitz continuity of the prox-gradient map via nonexpansiveness, giving the lim result (App. A)
BCMS19 stopping-time theorem for E[T_eps] (Thm 21)
Taylor expansion of ared-cred under common random numbers plus Markov gives N = O(Delta^-2) (Sec. 5)
experiments: 100 realisations each: l1-regularised 2-layer network on HIGGS vs Adam (same seeds, 150 vs 50 iterations; Adam wins as lambda -> 0); topology optimisation d = 20,000 vs deterministic proximal TR on SAA; histograms of test error and trust-region radius curves (pp. 23-28).
positioning: Extends STORM/BCMS19 and generalises Baraldi-Kouri; claims simpler assumptions than stochastic SQP and interior-point methods (convex constraints only); STORM chosen as the most general stochastic TR (pp. 1-3, 8-9).
writing: Abstract claims both recovery and simplification of STORM; Table 1 and Remarks 11-15 interpret the constants; explicit list of theory-vs-experiment deviations; conclusion contrasts stochastic and deterministic radius behaviour (pp. 1, 15-16, 24, 27-28).
limits_future: Convex phi with exact prox only; fixed TR update; alpha and beta not computable; experiments deviate from the assumptions; no high-probability bound; future: design rigorous yet practical stochastic inexactness conditions (pp. 2, 5, 16, 24, 28).

quotes.text: Via an improved analysis (which applies both to ProxSTORM and STORM) we make it evident that function estimates are utilized only via their differences - that is what we need to estimate if a function change rather than the function itself.
The value of λ is fixed in Figure 1, but we find that as the regularization parameter λ → 0, Adam outperforms ProxSTORM in the test error metric.
